description: Severe sea states (significant wave height Hs > 2.0m, peak swells > 4.0m) and gale winds during southwest monsoon enforce complete seasonal shutdown of offshore sand dredging at Daman, marine barge transport, and breakwater rock dumping from June 1 to September 30 (4 months annually).
evidence_text: Physical oceanographic data establishes that marine operations in open Arabian Sea are severely restricted during SW monsoon (June-September), with typical working window of 210 to 240 days per year.
notes: Documented seasonal operational window. Probability and numerical severity left as NULL to prevent fabrication.

scenario_name: Forest Clearance Delay for Captive Basalt Quarries
description: Primary captive quarries at Gargaon (Patch-1, 17.08 Ha) and Khanivade (Patch-5, 15.39 Ha) are located on classified government forest land. Mining cannot commence until Stage-I and Stage-II Forest Clearances are granted by MoEFCC under Forest (Conservation) Act 1980.
document_page: Gargaon Summary p7; Khanivade Summary p7
evidence_text: Lease areas are on Government Forest Land. Forest Clearance Stage-I applied and in process with MoEFCC and Maharashtra Forest Department.
notes: Statutory regulatory dependency. Halting clearance blocks extraction of 30.97 million tonnes of proved basalt reserves.

scenario_name: State Environmental Clearance Conditions for Hillock Quarries
description: Prior Environmental Clearance applications for Gargaon and Khanivade captive quarries are pending before SEIAA Maharashtra. Stringent blasting time restrictions, daily extraction caps, or public hearing litigation could constrain daily rock dispatch rates.
evidence_text: Public consultation proceedings document local community concerns regarding groundwater depletion, dust on orchards, and blasting vibrations, requiring mitigation compliance before EC grant.
notes: Statutory regulatory process. Probability and severity left as NULL.

scenario_name: Single Concession Dependency for Reclamation Sand
description: Port reclamation requires 80 million m3 of sand fill, entirely dependent on a single 102.77 sq.km offshore borrow polygon off Daman coast. Dredger breakdown, regulatory disputes with DNH & DD administration, or severe weather halts the entire filling operation with no viable onshore sand alternative.
evidence_text: Total sand requirement of 80 million m3 reserved under single statutory notification S.O. 5411(E) in offshore waters of Daman.
notes: High geographic concentration risk. Absence of alternative sand reserves documented.

scenario_name: Rural Road Haulage Bottleneck Prior to Expressway Completion
description: Haulage of 32.1 million tonnes of rock from Palghar quarries requires up to 2,000-3,000 truck trips per day. Existing SH-40, Dahanu-Jawhar road, and rural village roads have single/intermediate lane widths and weak culverts unable to sustain heavy tipper traffic prior to commissioning the 8-lane expressway.
document_page: Road DPR p20 Section 1.4, p93 Section 6.1; EIA p187
evidence_text: Existing road network consists of state highways and village roads with narrow carriageway, surface distress, and congested village junctions requiring a separate dedicated expressway.
notes: Operational and structural logistics bottleneck documented in Road DPR.

description: Very severe cyclonic storm (VSCS) in Arabian Sea generating 100-year return period waves (Hs = 6.8m to 7.2m, wave crests > 10m) during construction risks displacement of unfinished breakwater core, scour around reclamation perimeter bunds, and damage to floating equipment.
evidence_text: CWPRS technical reports 5581 and 5957 evaluated 100-year cyclone wave heights along breakwater alignment showing design significant wave height Hs of up to 6.8 m.
notes: Extreme meteorological event. Probability is not numerically assigned in sourcing context.

scenario_name: Western DFC Rail Link Construction Lag
description: Dedicated 28 km electrified rail link to New Palghar (Rs. 1,384.60 Cr) requires major bridges, rail flyover (RFO) across existing tracks, and land acquisition. Delay in commissioning shifts inbound cement, structural steel, and container evacuation onto congested highway networks.
document_page: Rail DPR p22 Section 0.5, p86 Section 13.3
evidence_text: Project includes complex railway flyover at New Palghar station and crossing of Western Railway main line, with 36-month construction duration for Phase 1.

scenario_name: Commercial Quarry Availability and Lease Life Expiry
description: Secondary identified quarries at Borsheti (8 acres), Kirat (6.5 acres), Nagzari (25 acres), and Girnoli are private commercial operations with small surface leases and competing regional construction demand. Lease expiry or local revenue moratorium could restrict third-party merchant stone availability.
document_page: DPR p72 Table 2-3; Road DPR p95 Table 7-3
evidence_text: DPR notes private quarry sites at Borsheti, Kirat, Nagzari, and Girnoli are actively being used for local construction; commercial reserve life and operating licenses require current verification.
notes: Identified fallback quarries require ground-truth verification prior to contract commitment.

description: CWPRS sedimentation numerical modeling indicates siltation rate of 0.5m in dredged basin (3.1 million m3 in non-monsoon alone). High post-monsoon silt accumulation can reduce draft for heavy aggregate barges and dredgers before maintenance dredging contracts are mobilized.
evidence_text: Studies reveal average rate of siltation in dredged area is about 0.5 m, with total quantum of likely siltation in dredged areas about 3.1 million cum for non-monsoon season only.
notes: Documented physical siltation phenomenon impacting marine navigation and logistics.
